channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
item.description: ActionOPD replaces offline imitation and token-level on-policy distillation with action-level on-policy distillation, rewarding student actions by semantic agreement with sampled teacher actions, so teacher token probabilities and shared tokenization are no longer required. It costs an on-policy RL training loop with sampling from both student and teacher at each state, which is substantially more compute- and orchestration-intensive than offline supervised fine-tuning, though the teacher can be a black-box API. It can fail if the sampled teacher actions are unrepresentative or the semantic-agreement reward is noisy, and the gains are demonstrated only on curated tool-use tasks, so transfer to other agent workloads is unverified. 2 independent implementations, 7 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LAGO: Language Agents with Reusable Growing Options
item.description: LAGO replaces a single monolithic tool-use loop, in which one agent must decompose, execute, and verify within one trajectory, with a meta-agent that retrieves or spawns specialized sub-agents stored as reusable options in a persistent library that grows across tasks without weight updates. The cost is orchestration complexity plus additional inference calls for meta-agent dispatch, verification, and admission of new options, since a frozen model is used in both roles and no training is required. It can fail when decomposition quality is poor, when the library accumulates mislabeled or non-transferable options, or when gains do not replicate across models and task distributions, as the ablation shows component contributions are task- and model-dependent. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Extremists Enter LLM Societies: Investigating Extreme Behavior in Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: EXAM replaces average-persona or fixed-scalar treatments of tail actors with LLM-native extremist agents whose proportion, spatial distribution, interaction protocol, and measurement interface are explicitly configured. It costs additional agents, prompt-history state, API tokens or GPU inference time, scenario-specific design, and repeated multi-round simulations rather than a single-model call. It can fail when results are backbone-dependent, prompt-brittle, protocol-sensitive, or when measured collective shifts are simulation artifacts rather than transferable production behavior. 1 independent implementation, 132 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Explorer-Zero: Improving Self-Play for Long-Horizon Tasks with Decomposable Verifiable Rewards
item.description: The method replaces human-annotated task datasets and binary-outcome verification with a learned proposer that generates tasks and records intermediate environment states as verifiable subtask checkpoints, trained jointly with a solver in alternating self-play RL. It costs an RL training pipeline with environment interaction, proposer-solver alternation, and multi-epoch rollouts, demonstrated at 30B scale, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU and likely requires substantial API or cloud compute budget. It can fail if the proposer generates unachievable or degenerate tasks, if recorded state checkpoints misalign with true subtask completion, or if alternating training destabilizes the curriculum. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Choosing the Number of Attention Heads from Intrinsic Dimension: A Small-Scale Study
item.description: The method replaces convention- or grid-search-based selection of attention head count with a label-free intrinsic-dimension estimate from a nested-dropout VAE, avoiding a hyperparameter sweep. The cost is a one-time VAE training pass over embeddings (here DistilBERT on WikiText-2) plus the assumption that the estimated dimension transfers to the target architecture; no inference-time overhead is added. It can fail because the evidence covers only two classification tasks and one small from-scratch 4-layer transformer, with no formal link between intrinsic dimension and head count, so the heuristic may not transfer to other tasks, sizes, or pretrained models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: STISA: A 0.16 GOPS/W/PE Single-Shot Inference FPGA-based SNN Accelerator with Algorithm and Hardware Co-Design
item.description: The method replaces multi-timestep SNN inference and prior SNN accelerator dataflows with Temporal Splitter Compression plus a co-designed FPGA architecture (TPOS mapping and Block-Mux Streaming). It costs FPGA development effort, model conversion into the TSS spiking form, and accuracy risk on harder tasks (ImageNet top-1 of 68.51% trails conventional CNN/Transformer baselines). It can fail if the target workload is not vision with event-driven tolerance, if the team lacks FPGA tooling and HLS/RTL expertise, or if accuracy degradation from timestep compression exceeds the application's threshold. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: A Strong Harness Narrows the Model Gap: A Comparative Evaluation for Legislative Document-to-XML Conversion
item.description: It replaces reliance on a stronger foundation model with deterministic tooling, task decomposition, and persisted per-agent state wrapped around a cheaper model. The cost is engineering complexity: building and maintaining the tool layer, orchestration logic, and schema validation rather than paying for a larger model. It can fail where the residual error lives outside the tools' reach, and the pipeline may not transfer to tasks lacking strict schemas or external authorities for deterministic lookup. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports
item.description: The method replaces trusting an agent's user-facing report as sufficient evidence of task state with systematic probing that compares what the report conveys against the full execution context. It costs an evaluation harness: recorded execution contexts, a question-generation and answering pipeline over ~37 tasks and thousands of probes, plus annotation or model-based scoring of supervision-relevant states, none of which requires training but does require API inference and engineering time. It can fail if probe questions are unrepresentative of real supervisory needs, if the model-based state assessment misfires on your domain, or if the measured gap does not translate into actionable intervention decisions. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The Code of Theseus: Can Agents Rebuild Software from Recovered Design Documents?
item.description: The method replaces manually written or absent requirements and architecture documents with artefacts recovered automatically from a static dependency graph and a few key files, avoiding the context-saturating full-code reading of prior approaches. Cost is one offline generation pass per repository plus judge-based validation; the recovered artefacts improved structural fidelity but produced no significant gain in test pass rate, so the functional benefit is unproven. It can fail because an LLM judge rated the artefacts less reliably correct and at the right abstraction level, meaning misleading design documents could steer agents toward plausible but wrong structures. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Designing Textual Interfaces To Enhance Llm Reasoning On Audio-Visual Question Answering
item.description: The method replaces ad-hoc manual prompting of omni-modal LLMs with automatic prompt optimization applied through deliberately designed textual interfaces (direct OmniLLM, captioner-reasoner, or agent-orchestrated subagents). It costs additional inference calls for the optimization loop and, for the decomposed variants, extra captioning and orchestration latency plus a more complex system to maintain. It can fail because gains are model-dependent, the interpretable interfaces are harder to optimize, and error propagation from the captioner or subagents can degrade answers after optimization. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: EvalBuilder: Can LLMs Build Efficient Benchmarks?
item.description: EvalBuilder replaces expensive, human-constructed reference benchmarks with LLM-agent-generated proxy benchmarks intended to preserve model rankings at lower cost. The cost is the compute and time budget spent running the benchmark-generation agent, plus the engineering effort to validate fidelity, robustness, and calibration of any generated proxy against the reference. It can fail if the proxy benchmark misranks held-out models or fresh responses, in which case adoption decisions rest on a distorted evaluation signal. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Why Generate a Click? Plug-in Decision Heads for Web Agents
item.description: The method replaces text-based action decoding (generating tokens like click(12)) with lightweight classification heads that read action type, target element, and text-option choices directly from the frozen generator's hidden states, falling back to full decoding from the same forward pass's KV cache when head confidence is low. Costs include training the heads on web-step data (the paper used 213k steps), an additional confidence-threshold hyperparameter per deployment, and up to 2 points of step-success regression on some benchmarks (GUIAct, MiniWoB++) under loose thresholds. Failures after adoption can come from miscalibrated confidence on out-of-distribution websites, from UI layouts whose element structure differs from training data, and from degradation of the generator itself if heads are trained jointly rather than on frozen weights (up to 4.9 points of generator step-success loss). 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents
item.description: It replaces model-written summary compaction (and rewording-based deterministic compaction) with a deterministic scheme that keeps user and assistant prose verbatim and explicitly flags where information was stripped. Cost is low in complexity and compute, but retaining verbatim text preserves less aggressively than summarization, so effective context capacity may be tighter and no extra latency figures are given. It can fail when verbatim retention crowds out needed context under heavy compaction, and the evidence rests on the authors' own benchmarks tied to the Pi coding agent, so transfer to other agents and workloads is unverified. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: KANLab: TensorFlow Playground for Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
item.description: KANLab replaces static explanations and ad hoc notebooks for teaching Kolmogorov-Arnold Network concepts with a browser-based interactive playground forked from TensorFlow Playground. It costs nothing computationally since it runs client-side in a compact 2D setting, but it deliberately omits residual connections and learnable scaling parameters, so it does not reflect modern KAN implementations. It cannot fail in production because it is an educational tool, not a deployable method; the only risk is forming intuitions about simplified KANs that do not transfer to real architectures. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Sparse Autoencoders for Mechanistic Interpretability in NLP: A Critical Survey of Recoverability, Interpretability, and Utility
item.description: The survey covers sparse autoencoders, which replace dense, polysemantic hidden activations with sparse feature dictionaries intended to be individually interpretable; it does not propose a new method but critically reviews 138 studies. Adoption costs include training a separate autoencoder per model layer, added storage and inference overhead, and evaluation complexity, all within a literature whose results the authors show depend heavily on design assumptions and evaluation settings. Failure modes documented in the survey include features that do not faithfully reconstruct activations, non-robust semantic interpretability, and weak or inconsistent evidence of behavioral utility in downstream interventions. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Optimizing Sparse Boolean Rule Networks using Mixed Integer Linear Programming
item.description: Replaces heuristic and SAT-based methods for learning compact Boolean rule classifiers with globally optimal MILP training of a fixed conjunctive-disjunctive network. Costs MILP solver time that grows with dataset size and network width, plus hyperparameter tuning of the accuracy-sparsity trade-off; no GPU is needed. Can fail on larger or high-dimensional tabular problems where MILP does not scale, and on tasks where binary-rule expressiveness is inadequate. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RM-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Generative Reward Models
item.description: RM-OPD replaces mixed-domain GRPO training of generative reward models with a two-stage pipeline: single-domain GRPO teacher training followed by routed on-policy distillation with domain reweighting into one student. The cost is substantial: multiple domain-specialist RL fine-tuning runs plus a distillation stage, requiring multi-GPU training capacity and per-domain preference data that a single 24 GB GPU setup cannot realistically supply. It can fail through residual cross-domain imbalance if reweighting is miscalibrated, teacher quality bottlenecks if any specialist undertrains, and reward hacking inherited from the teachers' supervision signal. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: TreeSpark: Learning to Draft the Trees You Verify for Speculative Decoding
item.description: TreeSpark replaces reference-conditioned drafter training in semi-autoregressive speculative decoding (DSpark) with parent-conditioned tree construction trained via survival NLL and a capped coverage hinge, reusing existing target distributions so no extra target forward passes are needed. The cost is a custom drafter training pipeline tied to a specific architecture and target model (Qwen3-4B/8B), plus added training complexity from replaying tree expansion, pruning, and packing. It can fail if the workload differs from the evaluated general and writing benchmarks, since acceptance-length gains depend on drafter-target alignment and may not transfer to other targets or to batched serving, where gains shrink to 12.6%-17.2%. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: HEM-Med: A Hierarchical Agentic Memory Framework for Safe Multi-Center Medication Recommendation
item.description: Replaces single-center medication-recommendation models and naive multi-center transfer learning with a hierarchical memory that separates cross-hospital clinical experience from hospital-specific prescribing residuals, plus a safety-aware set decoder handling drug-drug interactions and formulary constraints. Costs include maintaining per-patient attribution records and dual memory stores, added retrieval and decoding complexity, and dependence on multi-center EHR data that is difficult to obtain. Can fail through privacy and regulatory constraints on cross-institution clinical data, poor transfer when a hospital's residual patterns dominate, and safety decoding that cannot guarantee absence of contraindicated combinations in deployment. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Continual pretraining Prostate MRI ViT Encoder for task alignment
item.description: The method replaces direct fine-tuning of a pretrained ViT encoder by inserting an intermediate LoRA continual-pretraining stage on a related task (prostate MRI segmentation) to better align pretrained representations with downstream objectives. It costs an additional training stage, though LoRA keeps it feasible on a single 24 GB GPU, plus the engineering overhead of managing two-stage adaptation. It can fail to deliver gains, as improvement appeared in only half the evaluated tasks, and benefits may not transfer outside the prostate MRI domain or to tasks dissimilar from the continual-pretraining objective. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: P2Patch: Exploit-Guided Vulnerability Repair
item.description: P2Patch replaces single-pass vulnerability repair, where a patch is validated only against the evidence used to construct it, with an adversarial loop in which an exploitation agent generates new same-vulnerability exploits against each patched program and the final patch must block all accumulated proofs of vulnerability. The cost is multiple agent iterations per finding (exploitation plus patching per round) on third-party APIs, increasing token spend and end-to-end latency per CVE, plus infrastructure to run PoVs and maintain separate held-out evaluation oracles. It can fail when the exploitation agent cannot produce a working PoV for a vulnerability class, when accumulated repair requirements overfit to the generated exploits rather than the underlying flaw, and because absolute coverage gains are modest, the added cost may not pay off on low-severity findings. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Repairing Speech Access After Text Updates with Frozen Affine Fields
item.description: AFFIRM replaces retraining or refitting the speech-language model after a text update with a frozen, detachable affine correction applied to speech hidden states in a single pass. It costs an operator-training phase over paired speech and text states plus a small per-query conditioning computation, keeping the base checkpoint untouched. It can fail to outperform simpler baselines: on balanced synthetic PopQA it showed no established advantage over SALSA steering or low-rank ReFT, and steering methods can degrade when transferred across domains, as the matched SALSA variant did. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Long-Horizon RL Needs Muon
item.description: The method replaces synchronous multi-rollout RL post-training with standard optimizers by a single-rollout asynchronous recipe built around the Muon optimizer for long-horizon issue-resolution agents. It costs a full RL training pipeline: rollout generation infrastructure, policy gradient training with importance-sampling corrections, and auxiliary penalty tuning, none of which fits a single 24 GB GPU without significant scale-down. It can fail through instability of asynchronous updates with truncated importance ratios, sensitivity to penalty weighting, and unverified transfer of the recipe beyond the two evaluated model families. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Comparative Evaluation of Deep-Learning based DoA Estimators for Real-Time ISAC Beamforming
item.description: The method replaces classical subspace-based DoA estimation (e.g., MUSIC) with a regression CNN inside an SVD-beamforming ISAC pipeline. The cost is that the speedup at the estimation stage is progressively negated by the SVD beamforming step, which becomes the latency bottleneck, and a learned estimator requires training data matched to the antenna array and channel conditions. It can fail under distribution shift in array geometry, SNR, or multipath conditions not represented in training, and the end-to-end spectral-efficiency benefit collapses if the SVD stage is not also replaced. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Understanding NVIDIA Grace-Blackwell Unified Memory Through Placement-Controlled Microbenchmarks
item.description: This is a measurement study, not a deployable method: it replaces reliance on a single 'Unified Memory bandwidth' figure with a placement- and history-aware cost model covering local HBM access, host-mapped access, prefetch, reuse, migration, and oversubscription eviction. Adopting its guidance costs engineering effort in explicit placement and prefetch management of managed allocations, plus benchmarking on the target platform. It fails when workloads exceed CUDA-visible memory capacity (performance drops roughly 4-5x into eviction territory) or when its GB200-specific numbers are extrapolated to the different hardware the reader actually operates. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: From Relevance to Validity: Zero-Shot Tool Selection via Functional and Contextual Validation
item.description: The method replaces pure semantic relevance ranking for tool selection with a progressive pipeline that adds endpoint-grounded functional compatibility checks and task-conditioned contextual validation on top of retrieval. The cost is additional LLM calls per candidate tool for the functional and contextual validation stages, increasing selection latency and API spend, plus engineering effort to ground tool endpoints. It can fail when tool endpoint specifications are incomplete or inaccurate, when the validation LLM misjudges functional compatibility, and in domains where the contextual evidence it relies on does not transfer. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FOLD: Position-Free Far Memory with Local Order for Long-Context Speculative Decoding
item.description: FOLD replaces retraining or window-restriction of speculative drafters on long inputs by keeping exact local positions, collapsing distant KV entries into a far-memory at a shared position, and sharpening attention within it. It is training-free, so it costs no fine-tuning budget; the overhead is modified drafter attention logic and hyperparameters controlling far-memory sharpening and its weight versus the local window. It can fail through attention dilution on very long histories, sensitivity of the sharpening and weighting hyperparameters to workload, and gains that depend on having a compatible target-drafter speculative decoding stack already in production. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
item.description: The method replaces repeatedly supplying context at inference time (long prompts, retrieval, or ad-hoc fine-tuning) with offline distillation of context-conditioned behavior into mergeable low-rank or structural FFN weight updates, using prospective query generation to anticipate future uses of the context. It costs an offline training pipeline per context or edit batch (synthetic query generation, distillation passes, update merging and validation), which fits a single 24 GB GPU only for smaller backbones or via parameter-efficient setups, and it adds operational complexity for update versioning and rollback. It can fail when prospective queries do not cover actual downstream usage, when sequential updates accumulate interference and degrade non-target capabilities beyond the reported retention, and because the reported Pareto-frontier results come from the authors' own five-task testbed rather than independent production workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: HRTF Upsampling and Personalization via Neural Operators
item.description: SPARO replaces per-subject neural-field fitting and classical spherical-harmonic interpolation for HRTF upsampling with a single learned operator that encodes sparse measurements into spherical latent modes, processes them with Transformer blocks, and decodes at arbitrary query directions. The cost is training a domain-specific model on HRTF datasets such as SONICOM or HUTUBS plus the measurement apparatus needed to obtain the sparse per-subject samples, neither of which is an LLM-inference concern. It can fail on subjects or measurement geometries outside the training distribution, and its ITD error is only competitive rather than best, which matters for localization accuracy. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: From Training to Escalation: Forensic Analysis and Local Recreation of RL/RLHF-Induced Privilege Escalation in AI Agents (CVE-2026-65616)
item.description: The paper shows that privilege escalation in AI agent evaluations stemmed from misconfigured internal package repositories allowing cryptographic verification bypass and token forgery (CVE-2026-65616), and proposes replacing implicit-trust deployment setups with Zero Trust Architecture controls such as per-request authentication and strict verification. The cost is additional engineering complexity: hardened repository configurations, token validation enforcement, and isolated containerization rather than any GPU or compute overhead. What can fail is incomplete coverage, since Zero Trust controls only neutralize this attack vector if every internal service is consistently configured, and a single misconfigured endpoint reopens the shared exploit pattern. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: The COUNT: Counting N-grams Unlocks Scaling on Host Memory and Training-Free Adaptation
item.description: COUNT replaces learned n-gram embedding tables (trained from scratch on GPU) with precomputed corpus n-gram counts stored in host memory, which weight the LM's own unembedding rows to form embeddings with no additional learned parameters. It costs host RAM for the count table, preprocessing to build it, and an added embedding lookup per token; the benefit only materializes if the backbone is pretrained with COUNT as an input. It can fail for the reader because the gains are demonstrated only for models pretrained from scratch with the method, and no compatible pretrained checkpoint may exist; count tables can also be stale or mismatched to the target domain, degrading the training-free adaptation. 1 independent implementation, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN): An Analysis of Adaptive Action Grids in Decoupled Q-Learning
item.description: SGQN replaces uniform coarse-to-fine action-grid growth in decoupled value-based continuous control with an adaptive grid that adds bins near high-Q bins and prunes low-Q ones, using epsilon-greedy selection. It costs nothing extra in principle, but the paper's own ablation shows the adaptive grid activates all bins and behaves like uniform growth, pruning changes returns by at most 1.1%, and the real drivers are coarse initialization and epsilon-greedy exploration; it also uses one gradient update per environment step, an uncontrolled confound versus baselines. What can fail after adoption: the claimed benefit may not transfer, since the advantage cannot be attributed to the adaptive grid, an annealed softmax collapses returns by 23-100%, and fine-grid initialization produces collapsed seeds. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
item.description: AdaRSI replaces indiscriminate fine-tuning of every failing sub-step (or harness-only refinement of a frozen executor) with a failure-attribution loop: a coding agent retries failing sub-steps from saved states, distinguishes harness errors from capability gaps, and fine-tunes only the sub-steps that remain unreliable using self-collected demonstrations. The cost is substantial supporting infrastructure: a checkpointable simulator environment, a coding agent to manage the loop, state saving and replay, and repeated fine-tuning runs of a VLA executor, which is feasible on a single GPU only for modest models. Failure modes include misattribution of harness versus capability errors, low absolute success (13.8% on unseen composites) that limits production readiness, distribution shift from self-collected demonstrations, and dependence on a resettable simulation that most real-world deployments lack. 1 independent implementation, 227 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
item.description: ReaDy replaces the target-hidden-feature conditioning used by feature-based drafters (e.g., DSpark) with position-specific context retrieved from the target model's committed recurrent states via learned queries and a lightweight state reader. The cost is an additional adaptation stage, low-rank state readers, and fused operators on top of a hybrid linear attention target model, and the demonstrated results depend on a 27B-parameter model on an 80GB B200, which exceeds the reader's single 24GB GPU budget. It can fail for the reader because it applies only to HLA-architecture models, requires training the reader against a specific target, and its speedup is unvalidated at model sizes and hardware the reader can actually run. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
item.description: The method replaces clinician-adjudicated or purely structural ranking of discovered EHR disease-trajectory motifs with a two-level score combining embedding-based semantic sparsity against 166,972 PubMed references and reliability-adjusted clinical priority. It costs a one-time embedding and calibration pass over motif textualizations (feasible on a single GPU or CPU with bge-small-en-v1.5), but requires an upstream trajectory-discovery pipeline, MIMIC-IV-scale longitudinal EHR data, and a curated literature reference corpus. Hard top-k membership was unstable across encoders, templates, and score settings, the semantic score showed no monotonic forecasting benefit, and agreement with an independent RND baseline was low (q90 Jaccard = 0.125), so ranking decisions can shift under reasonable configuration changes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
item.description: The method replaces continuous long-horizon agent search (single-agent iteration, parallel agents, or communicating teams that accumulate full history) with periodic restarts: all agent sessions and candidate history are discarded and the search resumes from the best candidate found so far. It costs no extra compute or memory relative to the baseline strategies, since it operates at fixed budget, but adds orchestration logic for checkpointing best candidates, scheduling resets, and re-seeding agents; reset frequency becomes a new hyperparameter. It can fail when the discarded history contained information needed to escape the current basin, when the best-so-far candidate is a local optimum that restarts cannot leave, or when task verifiers are noisy enough that the retained candidate is misjudged; the reported gains are also limited to four specific open-ended tasks and may not transfer. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
item.description: CIPR augments standard SFT or RL post-training, where each sample is scored independently under one interface, with a self-supervised KL penalty between action distributions produced under two interface views of the same sample in which action names are replaced by uninformative identifiers. It costs the construction of paired interface views and an additional forward pass per training sample to compute the cross-interface KL, but adds no inference-time latency or memory overhead. It can fail when held-out perturbations fall outside the consistency structure learned during training, it recovers only part of the robustness gap (10.5 of roughly 25 points), and it is inapplicable to teams that consume models exclusively through inference APIs without fine-tuning access. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
item.description: Replaces one-shot KV-cache eviction/compression heuristics with a per-document learned compact cache, optimized via test-time training using generic prompts while model weights stay frozen. Costs a per-document training pass at inference time (extra latency and compute before serving, plus engineering complexity for the two-stage distillation procedure), though memory during generation drops by the compression factor. Can fail when the per-document training cost exceeds the cache savings (short documents, single-query workloads), when generic prompts fail to cover the information later questions require, or when serving infrastructure cannot amortize the per-document training across many queries. 1 independent implementation, 1 star. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
item.description: The method replaces demonstration-only supervised fine-tuning for game and computer-use control with SFT initialization followed by PPO in sixteen programmatically rewarded synthetic environments, plus an extended action space (relative pointer motion, sustained and composite inputs). The cost is building and maintaining the environment suite with verifiable rewards and randomized dynamics, and running multi-environment RL on 9B and 35B-class models, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU without substantial offloading or API-based training infrastructure. Transfer can fail when target games diverge from the synthetic environments' control demands, reward design can incentivize behaviors that do not generalize, and results are validated only on MineDojo, ViZDoom, and GameWorld rather than arbitrary commercial titles. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
item.description: The method replaces the need to select and deploy a fixed-size model variant (S/B/L) by converting one pre-trained transformer into an elastic model that serves a continuum of sparsity levels, using a differentiable relaxation that jointly ranks every MLP neuron and attention head on a common scale. It costs a short construction process (reported as minutes) plus validation per sparsity target; no retraining or weight correction is required, and storage of the original dense weights is preserved with structured units removed at serving time. Failure modes include steeper accuracy loss beyond the reported 60% sparsity regime, uneven behavior on tasks or model families outside the 27 evaluated encoders, and hardware-specific speedups that may not reproduce on the reader's GPU without structured-pruning-aware kernels. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Batch-Paced: Fixed-Budget Batch Decoding in Discrete Diffusion Language Models
item.description: Batch-Paced replaces per-sequence dLLM decoding schedules, which allocate compute independently per request, with a training-free joint allocation of a fixed decoding budget across a batch. It costs additional scheduling logic at the serving layer and optional quality trade-off when a decoding-depth allowance is used to shorten batch decode time, though reported decode time remains competitive. It fails if the serving stack runs autoregressive models rather than discrete diffusion LLMs, or at small batch sizes where the reported gains shrink. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Virtual Head Attention
item.description: VHA replaces standard GQA attention in a model trained from scratch, using a query premix and a low-rank I + AB^T postmix that fold into the query and output projections at inference, yielding a GQA-2-equivalent model with two KV heads. The cost is that the gains only exist if the architecture is adopted at pretraining time; it cannot be retrofitted onto existing pretrained checkpoints, and the reader has no pretraining budget. What can fail after adoption is unvalidated quality at scales or context lengths beyond the reported experiments, and the small accuracy deltas may not transfer to downstream fine-tuning or domain-specific workloads. 1 independent implementation, 5 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: BELT : BEhavior-Aligned Low-Rank KV Cache Compression with Learned Top-k Rank Allocation
item.description: BELT replaces the full-rank KV cache in a pretrained LLM with a low-rank factorized cache, where a learned allocator distributes a fixed component budget across layers and heads, and where the compression objective matches post-softmax attention distributions rather than raw keys. Adoption costs an offline training/calibration phase for the low-rank factors and rank allocator, integration of custom Triton kernels (or a custom attention path) into the inference stack, and additional engineering complexity around combining low-rank storage with quantization. It can fail when the learned rank allocation does not transfer to domains or sequence lengths outside its training distribution, when real long-context workloads lose the reported LongBench quality margin at aggressive budgets, or when kernel and serving-stack integration overhead erodes the reported throughput gains on the reader's single-GPU setup. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Neural Dimensional Analysis: Foundations of Dimensionless and Scale-Consistent Computation
item.description: The method replaces standard scale-control machinery (layer normalization, residual scaling, attention temperature, loss weighting) with a dimensional-consistency framework implemented as the Gauge-Canonical Transformer with normalized coordinates and orthogonalized residual additions. The cost is that benefits accrue only when training a model from scratch under this architecture, plus implementation complexity in reworking residual streams, attention inputs, and multi-loss objectives. It can fail to transfer if adopted piecemeal onto existing pretrained checkpoints, and its quantization-robustness and stability claims are demonstrated only up to 1B parameters on the authors' training setup. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: AlignPred: Error-Controlled KV Cache Compression via Alignment and Predictive Coding
item.description: AlignPred replaces storing raw or conventionally compressed persistent KV caches in multi-turn agent deployments with a codec that aligns heads/layers via local orthogonal transforms, predicts token-wise and cross-head/layer, then quantizes residuals on an error-bounded lattice with entropy coding, and it integrates with SGLang HiCache. The cost is added encode/decode compute in the serving path (CPU codec overhead, though reported as faster than baseline codecs), integration effort with a specific serving stack, and a configurable reconstruction-error budget that must be tuned per workload. Failure modes include quality degradation if the error budget is set too aggressively for tasks sensitive to KV fidelity, gains that may not transfer beyond the three evaluated attention mechanisms or the LongBench-Pro benchmark, and limited benefit for workloads without long-lived cross-session caches. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Exact power indices for plurality-voting ensembles
item.description: ENPOWER replaces Monte Carlo sampling approximations of Shapley/Banzhaf values for plurality-voting ensembles with exact closed-form and generating-function algorithms, applied to ensemble pruning and prompt-based ensembling of vision-language models. Cost is low: it is a post-hoc combinatorial computation requiring no GPU training, only the base classifiers' predictions, with polynomial-time complexity that grows with class count and ensemble size. It can fail when the plurality-voting-with-random-tie-breaking model does not match the production aggregation rule (e.g., weighted or soft voting), and attribution-driven pruning may remove classifiers whose value depends on correlated errors that power indices do not capture. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LatentRemedy: Efficient Remedy For Non-Prefix KV Cache Reuse in Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: It replaces selective recomputation and offset-based calibration for recovering quality when reusing non-prefix KV cache blocks across agents with conflicting tasks, substituting recomputation of the shared block with a few MLP-generated latent tokens inserted after the reused block. The cost is training a small MLP via full-prefill distillation per model, plus extra inference-time compute and engineering to insert latent tokens into the serving path. It can fail outside multi-agent workloads with genuinely shared context blocks, if the distillation training does not transfer to a different base model or task distribution, or if the serving stack cannot accommodate inserted latent tokens without modification. 0 independent implementations, 12 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ChampionKV: Head-Wise Adaptive Budget Allocation for KV Cache Compression
item.description: ChampionKV replaces the uniform or predefined per-head budget allocation in observation-window KV compressors (SnapKV, PyramidKV) with input-adaptive head-wise budgets derived from attention concentration, leaving the token-selection procedure unchanged. The cost is negligible compute overhead for computing aggregated observation-window attention scores, plus an abnormal-head mask and floor-budget mechanism, with no additional memory beyond the compressed cache itself. It can fail to deliver gains on 7B/8B-class models, where results are mixed, and it does not uniformly outperform Ada-KV's global cross-head Top-K selection, so the base compressor choice may dominate the improvement. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: H-DDCM: Hadamard Codebooks for Fast Generative Image and Video Compression
item.description: H-DDCM replaces the dense Gaussian codebooks of codebook-based training-free diffusion compression (e.g., Turbo-DDCM) with implicit randomized Hadamard dictionaries synthesized via the fast Walsh-Hadamard transform, and adds a table-free lexicographic scheme for combinatorial bitstream encoding. The cost is that encode/decode still runs full diffusion or flow-model inference per block, so end-to-end latency and quality remain bounded by the pretrained generator rather than by the codebook, and the method only pays off at ultra-low bitrates where perceptual, not distortion, metrics dominate. Adoption can fail if no suitable pretrained image/video diffusion model exists for the target domain, if rate-distortion (PSNR/SSIM) rather than perceptual quality is the requirement, or if the KV-cache re-encoding streaming scheme drifts on long videos. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Revisiting Error Feedback for Model Quantization
item.description: Replaces the fixed-order error-feedback coefficients used in GPTQ/LDLQ-style post-training quantization with coefficients optimized via a metric-dependent trace problem, attained by a geometric mean decomposition of the Hessian. Cost is limited: it runs as a modification to an existing one-shot PTQ procedure on a single GPU, with added complexity from computing downstream-sensitive metrics, and QAT variants require additional training budget. What can fail: the paper itself shows that minimizing the trace bound does not guarantee better finite-level (actual bit-width) quantization accuracy, so gains may not transfer to a specific model and task without validation. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SparPR: Runtime KV-Cache Recovery for Resource-Constrained LLM Inference on Consumer Hardware
item.description: SparPR replaces static KV-cache eviction policies (e.g., StreamingLLM, H2O) and full offloading/reload in FlexGen-style constrained inference with runtime query-aware block selection, dynamic cache budgeting, and on-demand local recomputation with a cost-aware fallback to full recovery, requiring no weight changes or offline training. Its cost is runtime overhead for scoring, cost estimation, and selective recomputation, plus implementation complexity tied to the FlexGen/FlexLLMGen stack. It can fail if the runtime cost model mispredicts copy-versus-recompute tradeoffs on different hardware, if query-aware selection drops blocks needed by later tokens in workloads unlike the Needle benchmark, or if gains measured on an 8GB laptop do not transfer to a 24 GB production GPU serving different models and request patterns. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SimInter: Evidence-Grounded User Simulation with Interview-Based Profile Enrichment for Conversational Recommender Systems
item.description: SimInter replaces user simulators conditioned only on ratings, demographics, and static profiles by enriching profiles through synthetic LLM interviews grounded in historical conversational evidence, with a turn-level audit agent flagging fabrication and stereotyping. The cost is additional LLM inference for interview generation and auditing per simulated user, plus pipeline complexity; it is feasible on API access or a single GPU, but the paper validates only movie recommendation on ReDial, so transfer to other domains is unverified. After adoption, the main failure mode is residual fabricated or stereotyped attributes passing the audit (about 5.7% of claims unsupported and 4.8% auditor disagreement), which can bias downstream recommender evaluation. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Jev-Guard: Fast Routing and Auditing Agent Actions over Editable Policy Trees
item.description: Replaces an autoregressive guardrail model or LLM-as-judge used for agent action auditing with a single small model that first routes over an editable policy tree and then classifies safety conditioned on the retrieved policy. Costs include training or obtaining the specialized model, maintaining the policy tree spanning moderation, cybersecurity, privacy, and legal domains, and a residual error rate of roughly 6% on both routing and classification; integration is demonstrated only within the Hermes harness. Can fail through misrouting to the wrong policy branch (which invalidates the downstream audit), residual misclassification of unsafe actions, and policy drift if the editable tree is not kept synchronized with actual deployment rules. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Let the Mind Conceive, Let the Hand Achieve: Following Multimodal Instructions for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
item.description: Orchestra replaces monolithic end-to-end action policies for multi-step robot instructions with a harness that decomposes instructions into ordered subtasks, maintains shared spatial and progress context, and uses a separately trained progress evaluator to decide when to advance. The cost is added system complexity: a planner, context tracking, and a separately trained progress evaluator on top of the action policy, plus dependence on the underlying pi_0.5-style policy. It can fail when the progress evaluator misjudges subtask completion, when object-location tracking drifts as the scene changes, or when the base action policy cannot execute a decomposed subtask it was not trained on. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes
item.description: Urbex replaces candidate-ranking pipelines that depend on precomputed 3D instance proposals with a VLM agent that actively navigates a multi-view city scene (querying landmarks, zooming, rendering oblique views) before committing a bounding box, trained with reinforcement learning on CityRefer. The cost is an interactive multi-view rendering environment, RL training of the tool-use policy with localization and shaping rewards, and a VLM agent capable of sequential spatial reasoning, none of which is off-the-shelf for a constrained-infrastructure team. Failure modes include the agent committing to a wrong region during search, degraded performance on scenes whose geometry or landmark distribution differs from CityRefer, and environment/rendering engineering overhead that may exceed the cost of a simpler ranking baseline for smaller scenes. 2 independent implementations, 76 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Teacher-Guided Tool Learning for Small Language Models via Bidirectional KL Constraints
item.description: The method replaces pure reinforcement learning and direct teacher supervision (SFT/distillation) for training small language models to use external tools, combining reverse-KL token-level teacher feedback on low-reward trajectories with forward-KL demonstration supervision. It costs a capable teacher model accessible during training, RL training infrastructure, and added implementation complexity over plain SFT or distillation. Adoption can fail if the teacher's tool-use preferences contain errors that persist through forward-KL supervision, if the reader lacks RL training capacity on a single 24 GB GPU, or if results on BFCL v4 and API-Bank do not transfer to the reader's specific tool schemas and APIs. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Readout Scaling Shapes Sparse Feature Recovery
item.description: RC-DS replaces standard centered-logit SAE training coordinates with coordinates canonicalized to remove readout singular-value gains while preserving decision information. It costs an additional coordinate transformation (available as an exact wrapper) and, per the paper's own controls, worse output-logit reconstruction than centered-logit SAEs in most tested settings. It can fail when the generating distribution differs from the assumed pre-readout space, since the benefit reverses with the data distribution, and reconstruction gains do not imply task-useful features, as the label-detection and steering controls indicate. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ProTok: Unified Protein Tokenization via Modular Multi-Codebook Quantization
item.description: ProTok replaces separate per-modality protein tokenizers (independent sequence, structure, and function vocabularies) with a single modular multi-codebook product-quantized vocabulary that supports inference from any modality subset without retraining. Adoption costs the training of a new tokenizer and any downstream model over its tokens, plus integration of a non-standard vocabulary; reconstruction quality (0.939 lDDT) and multi-modal fusion add pipeline complexity relative to single-modality tokenizers. Failure modes include degraded performance on out-of-distribution proteins, dependence on the availability and quality of structural and functional annotations, and benchmark gains that may not transfer to a specific downstream design or retrieval workload. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Judges Follow the Reference: The Derivation Gap in Verifying Tool-Call Arguments
item.description: DeRef replaces giving the judge raw (possibly truncated or reference-free) conversation history by having a separate model read the full history without seeing the candidate argument and write an explicit reference stating what the value should be. It costs one additional model inference per judged argument, adding latency, API or GPU cost, and a new pipeline component. It can fail when the reference-writing model itself misderives the intended value, since judges are shown to follow the visible reference even when it is incorrect, so a wrong reference can systematically flip verdicts. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: The Last Mile of Coding Agents for Long-Document Tasks: An Empirical Study on Clinical Trial Protocol Digitization
item.description: The technique replaces a generic coding-agent harness (and reliance on frontier proprietary models) with a domain-specific harness that adds task skills and a verification loop for long-document-to-structured-output tasks. The cost is engineering effort to build domain skills and verifiers, plus extra verification passes that increase token consumption and latency, and the reported gains are measured only on clinical trial protocol digitization. After adoption, agents can still fail in the transcription and structuring stage, so structured outputs require downstream validation, and the skill assets may not transfer to other document domains without rework. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Two For The Price Of One: Curvature-Aware Pruning Preserves Influence Functions Too
item.description: CACTUS replaces standard post-training pruning solvers (and the LLM-Surgeon optimizer) with an ADMM-based method that jointly matches layer activations and backpropagated gradients, supporting both pruning and sparse-plus-low-rank decompositions. It costs a calibration optimization pass per layer, added implementation complexity over magnitude or WANDA-style pruning, and optionally memory for the low-rank correction term. It can fail if the calibration data is unrepresentative of deployment inputs, if the target hardware lacks sparse-kernel support to realize 2:4 speedups, or if influence-function preservation does not transfer to tasks beyond the evaluated data-selection and perplexity settings. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Lost in Implicit Routing: How LLM Agents Fail to Load Relevant Skills at Scale
item.description: Explicit preselection of relevant skills before agent execution replaces implicit routing, in which the agent scans full skill metadata and decides what to load during the task. It costs an additional selection step with its own latency and coverage trade-offs, and requires a mechanism (retriever or selector model) to pick candidate skills from the library. It can fail when the preselector misses the golden skill, since the agent then has no opportunity to recover it, and gains shrink when libraries are small enough that implicit routing has not yet collapsed. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Reading Right, Acting Wrong: Diagnosing Decision Failures of System One Models in Agent Loops
item.description: The method replaces uninterpretable single-pass action scoring with behavioral diagnostics: each next-action decision is paired with independent factual probes about the same state, separating perception failures from decision failures and enabling a repair path where the model's own correct factual answers are composed by code to fix the action. It costs additional probe queries per decision state, benchmark construction effort, and code to compose answers, adding latency and engineering complexity to the evaluation loop. It can fail when the diagnosis relies on synthetic probes that do not transfer to production states, and the abstract notes that on real states the missing element is often the next sub-goal, which factual probing and code composition may not supply. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Does self-distillation improve reasoning?
item.description: Self-distillation (SDPO, OPSD) trains a model to imitate its own predictions conditioned on privileged information, positioned as a more sample-efficient replacement for reinforcement learning from rewards; this paper is a critical re-evaluation, not a new method. The method costs a training run with privileged conditioning and adds distillation pipeline complexity over standard supervised fine-tuning, while this paper finds its gradients align weakly with reward-optimizing policy gradients. What can fail: reported gains do not transfer to unseen problems, are explained by overfitting or transferring existing behavior rather than using privileged information, and so the approach may deliver no out-of-distribution improvement in production. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Can an Agent Learn to Predict Its Own Failure? Outcome-Grounded Confidence Calibration in LLM Agents
item.description: The method replaces self-reported verbalized confidence calibrated only against per-step correctness with RL-calibrated per-step confidence scored against eventual episode outcome, using GRPO group rollouts as success labels and a proper scoring rule. It costs a GRPO training run (offline on recorded trajectories or online on the live agent) on a 7B model, plus instrumentation to log per-step confidence, fitting a single 24 GB GPU but requiring RL pipeline engineering. It can fail when confidence must distinguish a failing from a succeeding attempt on the same task, since gains concentrate on first-step task-level foresight rather than within-task discrimination, and results are confined to ALFWorld, TextWorld, and WebShop with Qwen2.5-7B. 0 independent implementations, 122 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Knowledge Graphs as Files: An Agent Harness Where Tool Creation and Tool Use Co-Evolve
item.description: It replaces predefined graph query interfaces and fixed retrieval tools with an agent that writes and revises Python code directly over complete node and edge files, interleaved with shell search. The cost is higher per-query LLM token consumption and multi-turn code execution latency, plus an execution sandbox and the requirement that the knowledge graph be available as flat files. It can fail when the model writes incorrect or inefficient code over large node sets, when graphs exceed practical file-inspection sizes, or when unconstrained code execution introduces security and reproducibility risks in production. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MultiAlloc: Budget-Aware Precision Allocation for KV Cache Quantization
item.description: It replaces fixed-granularity KV cache quantization policies (uniform layer-wise or token-wise precision assignment) with a profiling-guided allocator that splits a fixed KV memory budget between layer-wise precision enhancement and token-wise preservation. The cost is a one-time offline profiling pass to estimate layer sensitivity and token importance, plus implementation complexity for mixed-granularity quantization; there is no online search overhead at inference. It can fail if the profiling distribution diverges from production traffic (token-importance and layer-sensitivity estimates may not transfer), if the serving stack lacks kernels supporting mixed per-layer and per-token precision, or if the abstract's unquantified gains do not replicate on the reader's model and workload. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Kwai Summary Attention V2 Technical Report
item.description: KSA V2 replaces rigid same-window summary-token interleaving with summary tokens that act both as KV memory and sparse indexers, allowing per-layer compression windows and cheaper full-attention layers. It costs architectural modification and training from scratch or substantial fine-tuning, plus added serving complexity in the KV cache path, with unverified quality at long contexts. It can fail through degraded recall of distant exact content under aggressive per-layer compression and through implementation mismatch with standard inference stacks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Model-Based Online Decision Making via Generative Trajectory Planning
item.description: GTP replaces from-scratch trajectory optimization at every decision step by sampling action sequences from a learned diffusion prior and refining them with learned dynamics, reward, and value models. The cost is training and maintaining four learned components (diffusion proposal, dynamics, reward, value) plus sampling-and-refinement overhead at inference, which exceeds the compute profile of a single policy forward pass. Failure modes include compounding model error in the learned dynamics over long horizons, proposal distribution mismatch when deployment states drift from training data, and degradation in environments where reward or dynamics are hard to model accurately. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
item.description: ProAS replaces the uniform trajectory-level advantage broadcast of critic-free RL methods such as GRPO with fine-grained credit assignment, using a dynamically built Agentic Reference Graph to mask rewards for invalid actions in successful trajectories and redistribute penalties to early pivotal errors in failed ones. It adds no critic network but requires constructing and maintaining the reference graph during training, which adds implementation complexity and a graph-quality dependency on top of an already compute-intensive RL loop. It can fail if the reference graph is poorly constructed or unrepresentative of the task distribution, and although the authors report robustness to distilled or imperfect graphs, gains were demonstrated only on two benchmarks with small models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Knowing the User Is Not Knowing What We Established: Grounding Awareness in Personal Agents
item.description: It replaces treating remembered proposals or preferences as authorized instructions by adding an explicit grounding-status layer for accepted, unacknowledged, revised, and scoped arrangements before consequential actions. The cost is additional state tracking, action instrumentation, retrieval/check latency, and policy complexity rather than model retraining or extra GPU capacity. It can fail if grounding labels are wrong or stale, scope boundaries are missed, checks are not wired to all consequential tools, or conservative blocking reduces task completion. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Just Respect the Semantics: Image-Token Compression via Pre-LLM Semantic Variable-Resolution Tokenization and In-LLM Relevance Pruning
item.description: Varest replaces uniform full-resolution image tokenization feeding a VLM with pre-LLM variable-resolution merging guided by object and text localizers, plus learned [REL] registers that prune tokens after early decoder layers. It costs a training run per backbone (a single checkpoint covers multiple budgets) and adds localizer models and merging logic to the inference pipeline, so it is not a drop-in method unless pretrained checkpoints are released. It can fail on tasks requiring fine-grained text or small-object detail if localizers miss regions, and the 7-14% quality gap versus full tokens may be unacceptable for OCR-heavy or high-precision workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SP$^2$ec: Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
item.description: SP2ec replaces fixed draft configurations in self-speculative VLM decoding with a training-free bandit that selects the draft configuration per prompt during generation. It costs a small exploration overhead (bounded by a wall-time regret guarantee) and added implementation complexity on top of an existing self-speculative stack such as SWIFT or SpecVLM; no extra model training or memory for a separate drafter is required. It can fail if the assumed single-peak throughput pattern does not hold for a given workload, and the measured 11% ceiling means gains are marginal relative to the integration effort unless self-speculative decoding is already deployed. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts
item.description: SolBehave replaces compile-only and ad hoc unit-test evaluation of LLM-generated Solidity with three behavioral checks: differential fuzzing against the original contract, historical on-chain transaction replay, and DCR-graph-guided synthetic call-sequence replay. The cost is evaluation infrastructure: a reproducible EVM execution environment, transaction traces, and non-trivial compute and engineering effort to run differential and replay testing at scale. It can fail through incomplete behavioral coverage (fuzzers and DCR graphs miss divergence paths), oracle dependence on the original contract's behavior (which may itself be buggy or diverge in acceptable ways), and limited transfer to settings where no reference implementation or transaction history exists. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SEAR: Self-Evolving Agentic Robotics
item.description: SEAR replaces hand-tuned, single-attempt robot control pipelines with language-model agents that iteratively write control code, act in the loop, or fine-tune VLA models, retaining reusable skills across tasks; the accompanying benchmark replaces ad-hoc agent evaluation with controls that separate genuine retained learning from repeated retries, budget, and luck. The cost is substantial: running it requires simulation environments and optionally physical robots, large agent runtime budgets (the paper reports years of cumulative runtime), and frontier-model API spend that scales with task difficulty. What can fail is transfer: task-specific solutions do not generalize across tasks, simulators, or to novel human-designed real-robot scenes, so retained skills may be narrower than raw success curves suggest. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks
item.description: RoboSimStudio replaces ad-hoc, hand-tuned physics configuration for robot manipulation simulation with an interactive toolkit built on the Newton simulator that exposes solver, contact model, and physical parameters as explicit, editable choices for humans or coding agents. Its cost is engineering time in iterative visual, force-feedback, or agent-in-the-loop refinement, plus the infrastructure and hardware access required to run physics simulation and compare against real robot behavior; it does not consume inference GPU budget in the LLM-serving sense. It can fail where contact mechanics, friction, and deformation remain mis-modeled despite parameter editing, producing sim2real transfer gaps, and the abstract provides no quantified evidence of improved transfer accuracy or reduced tuning effort. 2 independent implementations, 17 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: The Last Remote Sensing Model Built by Humans? Casting Any Earth Observation Task as Recursive Self-Improvement
item.description: It replaces hand-designed EO training recipes and per-task expert tuning with a general-purpose coding agent that, given only a harness and a verifier, builds the model and recursively improves it against the verifier. The cost is sustained agent API spend plus many local training and evaluation runs on the single GPU, together with the engineering effort to construct a verifier and harness that genuinely reflect the production objective. It can fail by overfitting or gaming the verifier, leaking benchmark information through its own search, emitting non-reproducible artifacts, or running unbounded improvement loops that exhaust API and compute budget without off-benchmark gains. 0 independent implementations, 9 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
item.description: Replaces purely text-based chain-of-thought and tool interaction in LLM agents with a unified generation process that alternates between latent reasoning (via a HybridLink module and continuous working memory) and text-based tool calls, reducing tokens and latency. Costs include training the HybridLink plus two post-training stages (HybridSFT and HybridRL), added architectural complexity over standard prompting or ReAct-style loops, and dependence on a custom serving path rather than off-the-shelf API inference. Failure modes include coordination errors at latent-text transition points, degraded interpretability if latent thoughts are inspected only superficially, and results that may not transfer when applied to backbones or tool schemas different from those used in the paper's training. 1 independent implementation, 20 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
item.description: Replaces per-model training for CoT compression, steering-vector methods, and heuristic early stopping by adding a scaled logit difference from a small model run twice (brief-prompted vs verbose-prompted) to the large model's logits at every decoding step. Costs two extra small-model forward passes per generated token plus per-step logit manipulation, which roughly triples inference compute per token even though total tokens fall, so net latency and cost savings depend on the small model being much cheaper than the large one. Can fail if the steering strength is mis-tuned (accuracy degradation on tasks needing extended verification), if no suitable smaller reasoning model in the same family is available, or on workloads where the claimed accuracy parity does not transfer. 1 independent implementation, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
item.description: ChunkAct replaces per-primitive LLM reasoning over full interaction history with offline-compiled chunks of chained primitives that execute autonomously and return control to the planner only on failure, making LLM cost scale with decisions rather than primitive count. The cost is an offline compilation step that converts the agent's memory into chunks, plus loss of per-step planner oversight, since execution becomes memory-free between decisions. It can fail when a sub-goal's routine does not match the compiled chunk, when failure detection within a chunk is unreliable, or when tasks require mid-primitive replanning that the chunk structure cannot express. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SanSi: A Looped Typed Decision Model for System 1.5 Thinking
item.description: SanSi replaces generated chain-of-thought reasoning and large single-pass classifiers with a small looped language model that recursively re-applies its layers before a single typed readout, with one model serving any compute budget from one to eight loops. It costs a looped pre-trained backbone, multi-loop training with a proper scoring rule, and up to 8x the forward-pass latency of a single-pass model, though with no KV growth from generated tokens. It can fail on tasks needing explicit intermediate text, on decision formats outside the declared-option setting, or if the reported gains do not transfer from the paper's 59-source benchmark to the reader's domain, and adopting it requires reproducing the authors' specific training recipe rather than fine-tuning an off-the-shelf model. 0 independent implementations, 2 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: TRACE: Rollout-Guided Quantization-Aware Training for FP4 Reinforcement Learning of MoE Language Models
item.description: TRACE replaces independent train-side and rollout-side FP4 quantization in RL post-training with rollout-guided quantization-aware training that aligns the two quantized execution paths, plus a caching scheme that selectively stores mantissa and scale data from deeper layers. It costs additional training-time machinery: quantization-information caching and communication between rollout and training paths, implementation complexity in the RL stack, and reliance on FP4-capable hardware to realize the speedup. It can fail if the target hardware lacks native FP4 support (negating throughput gains), if the workload is inference rather than RL training (where the method does not apply), or if train-rollout discrepancy is not the accuracy bottleneck in the reader's setting. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: APEX: Speculate smarter, not deeper
item.description: It replaces fixed speculative decoding configurations (a single drafting method and a constant draft depth) with a request-level router among EAGLE-3, n-gram, and draft-model speculation plus block-level depth adaptation driven by verifier feedback. It costs training and maintenance of a learned survival-model controller, integration changes in the serving stack (vLLM), and the presence of multiple draft mechanisms resident in memory, though the target model and its verification procedure are unchanged. It can fail when controller signals mispredict acceptance on out-of-distribution workloads, when EAGLE-3 or draft-model heads are unavailable for the deployed model, or when the speedup does not transfer from the reported Qwen3-8B setup to other models or traffic mixes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Quantization Effects on Tool-Failure Recovery Vary Across Prompts and Evaluation Designs
item.description: This replaces ad hoc robustness evaluation (single prompt, fault-screened task subsets, implicit scoring policy) with a protocol requiring matched-task comparison, full-pipeline success reporting, stated scoring policies, and task-level uncertainty quantification. It costs additional evaluation runs across multiple prompts and scoring variants, plus the effort to rerun logs under different executor leniency settings; it requires no new infrastructure beyond what an engineer already uses for offline benchmarking. It can fail if treated as a one-time checklist: the paper shows conclusions reverse across prompts and scoring policies, so a deployment decision based on a single configuration remains unreliable even after adopting the protocol partially. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Persistent Memory in Multi-Agent LLM Inference: What It Costs, What It Buys, and When You Can Tell
item.description: A persistent memory tier storing and recalling reasoning traces replaces per-call re-derivation of intermediate reasoning, layered on top of multi-agent decomposition that bounds the active KV cache. It costs +0.368 MiB of peak cache per query plus the engineering complexity of trace storage, retrieval, and mandatory state reset between independent queries, with no measured accuracy benefit on single-question benchmarks. It fails when tasks supply their own evidence and are scored independently, since recalled traces then contain nothing informative, and poorly controlled ablations can hide this null behind measurement artifacts. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Do I Need the Cloud? Uncertainty-Aware Step-Level Handoff for Small Language Model Agents
item.description: Replaces once-per-query model routing (or always-on cloud inference for agents) with per-step uncertainty scoring that escalates only difficult agent actions from a local SLM to a stronger backend. Costs a scoring/escalation mechanism per step, roughly 30% cloud action volume, and the engineering complexity of maintaining two model backends plus threshold calibration. Can fail if the uncertainty signal miscalibrates on out-of-distribution tasks, since evidence comes from one model family, one stronger backend, scripted tasks, and small test sets. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Nucleus Speculative Decoding: Plausibility-Aware Verification Beyond Exact Distribution
item.description: NSD replaces the standard exact-distribution acceptance rule in speculative decoding with a relaxed rule that also accepts draft tokens inside the target model's nucleus. It costs no extra model or memory beyond an existing draft-target setup, but introduces bounded distributional deviation that scales with the draft's excess probability inside the target nucleus and can accumulate across the sequence. It can fail when the relaxed acceptance degrades output quality on distribution-sensitive tasks, so fidelity on the actual workload must be validated before production use. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.
