item.title: Lost in the bf16 Cast: Exporting Ternary Language Models Can Revert Most Low-Learning-Rate Code Changes
item.description: The technique replaces the standard ternary export path (cast latent weights to bf16, then requantize with the stock exporter) with either writing the training quantizer's codes directly or adjusting bf16 inputs so unchanged tools emit the correct codes. It costs nothing in memory, latency, or model quality; the only cost is a small modification to the export/save pipeline and a validation pass comparing exported codes against the training quantizer. What can fail: teams unaware of the issue may ship silently corrupted models, since bf16 rounding maps near-threshold values to zero and can revert most low-learning-rate fine-tuning changes, and the fix only matters if the reader actually fine-tunes or exports ternary models such as BitNet, Falcon-E, or BitCPM. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Tram-FL: Reducing Communication and Computation Costs through Sequential Model Circulation in Decentralized Federated Learning
item.description: Tram-FL replaces conventional decentralized federated learning, where every client holds a model copy, updates it locally, and exchanges and aggregates copies, with a single model circulated sequentially among nodes along a scheduled route with allocated update iterations and quantized momentum. The cost is the loss of parallel client computation: training is serialized over the circulation route, so wall-clock training time grows with the number of nodes, and the mechanism requires solving a scheduling problem for route and iteration allocation plus implementing quantized momentum. It can fail through slow convergence on a poorly chosen circulation schedule, sensitivity to node stragglers or dropouts since the single circulating model is a serialization point, and irrelevance outside federated settings since the method presumes distributed data ownership that most production teams do not have. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: ReFold: Training-Free Reversible Inter-Turn Context Folding for Long-Horizon Agents
item.description: ReFold replaces predictive context-management methods (auxiliary model calls, heuristic rules, or trained compression policies) with a training-free rendering layer that stubs content already displayed in earlier turns and folds agent-reported-finished turns into one-line notes, using chunked rendering that rewrites the cached prefix only every few steps. It costs implementation effort in the prompt-rendering layer of the harness and occasional one-step restores from the preserved history when a removal proves wrong, plus minor prefix-cache rewrites at chunk boundaries. It can fail when the agent incorrectly marks a turn as finished and later needs its details, requiring restores that add latency, and the reported gains may not transfer to workloads with low inter-turn redundancy or non-ReAct harness structures. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: ApexQuant: Data-Free Elastic Quantization by Residual Re-Isotropization
item.description: ApexQuant replaces calibration-data-dependent post-training quantizers with a calibration-free residual re-quantization scheme that stacks scalar, E8, or trellis stages so one artifact serves multiple bit-widths. It costs extra passes of encoding and decoding (latency and storage of multiple residual codes per layer), adds implementation complexity on top of an existing quantizer, and trades a small quality gap versus full precision. It can fail if the isotropization theory does not hold for particular layer distributions, if the two-bit quality still proves insufficient for the reader's downstream tasks, or if inference frameworks lack fast kernels for the multi-stage codebooks, negating the memory savings in practice. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: HE-OFT: Privacy-Preserving One-Shot Federated Fine-Tuning under Homomorphic Encryption
item.description: HE-OFT replaces standard federated fine-tuning, in which participants exchange model or gradient updates and all receive the trained model, with a one-shot protocol where clients upload a single CKKS-encrypted classifier-head displacement over a frozen backbone and no party obtains the final model. The cost is severe: per-query inference takes 443-1713 s on one CPU core (56-255 s with GPU level restoration), accuracy falls to 61-79%, and the approach is restricted to low-rank adapters plus a head on text or vision classification. It can fail through the 4-15 point accuracy loss versus a disclosed model, the operational burden of multiparty CKKS key management and quorum decryption, and infeasible latency for any interactive production workload. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: The Harness as the Only Mutable Surface: Compliance-Bounded Self-Evolution of LLM Agents in Credit Pipelines, with a Measured Admission Gate
item.description: The method replaces unconstrained self-modification of an agent (or no adaptation at all) with a dual-loop engine that confines all adaptation to the runtime harness—prompts, tool-call logic, primitive composition—while keeping model weights fixed, and admits changes only through a hash-chained, test-backed audit gate. The cost is substantial governance machinery: a proposer, replay against relabelled history, an admission record per change, and the requirement that any supervisory re-interpretation be encoded as an explicit relabelling rule, since the gate rejects everything evaluated on pre-shift labels. It can fail on structural shifts, where the gate's fixed tolerance blocked the correct primitive replacement in half the seeds at high severity, and all results come from a simulated agent with a seeded-search proposer rather than real language models. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: BRANCH: Bypassing Multi-Scanner AI Guardrails
item.description: BRANCH replaces single-scanner adversarial perturbation methods with a branching tree search that perturbs individual scanners while optimizing against the combined guardrail verdict. It costs attack-side compute and query budget (reported as lower than prior techniques) and, for a defensive adopter, implementing equivalent evaluation requires building a multi-scanner test harness. For the reader it can fail because its results demonstrate that deployed guardrail stacks, including commercial ones, are bypassable, so any production reliance on scanner-based guardrails alone leaves residual jailbreak risk. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: CORAL-KV: Compact Cross-Layer Prediction and Residual Coding for Autoregressive Video KV Caches
item.description: Coral-KV replaces clustering-based video KV-cache quantization (e.g., QVG-4/QVG-Pro) with cross-layer prediction: compact block-diagonal-plus-low-rank predictors estimate keys and values in later layers from earlier cache states, and only the residuals are quantized. The cost is fitting and storing the predictors, an optional per-video refit of block-diagonal components for higher fidelity, and added implementation complexity, with latency reported as comparable to baselines. It can fail if cross-layer dependencies are weak in a different model architecture, if residual coding error still compounds over very long generations, or if the reusable predictors do not transfer to videos outside the calibration distribution. 1 independent implementation, 25 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CircuitTree: Composing Circuits into A Syllable Transcriber
item.description: CircuitTree replaces a monolithic task-specific model with a hierarchy composed from many small subnetworks pruned out of a pretrained backbone (HuBERT), each circuit handling an identifiable subtask such as single-phoneme classification. The cost is a dedicated circuit-discovery and pruning pipeline, a greedy density-scaled composition procedure with Theta(N log N) scheduling overhead, and a small residual quality gap (1.2 accuracy points) against a non-composed ceiling. Adoption can fail when source circuits do not decompose cleanly for the target domain, when greedy composition propagates interference between circuits, or when the interpretability benefit does not justify the engineering effort over simply fine-tuning a small model. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Behind-the-Meter Photovoltaic Visibility from Net Smart Meters: Deployment Regimes and Operational Insights
item.description: This replaces unmonitored behind-the-meter PV estimation or per-site hardware telemetry with deep sequence models applied to existing net smart-meter data, evaluated under deployment regimes that separate household transfer from temporal extrapolation. It costs a training pipeline per deployment regime, labeled PV data for source and (minimally five-household) target supervision, plus context-length selection, rather than additional metering hardware. It can fail when deployed on unseen households or new regions without fine-tuning, since the deployment regime drives error more than model choice and transfer error is roughly 78% higher than seen-household error. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
item.description: SWE-Duel replaces static, leak-prone coding benchmarks (e.g., SWE-bench-style fixed task sets) with evaluation-time task generation, where agents alternately author buggy pull requests and review each other's under mirrored Red-Blue turns with test-based oracles. The cost is substantial: each turn requires three context-isolated Red sessions plus a blind repair check and a Blue review, and the reported tournament ran 1,500 turns across 11 frontier model-harness pairs, which is entirely API- or compute-billed agent execution rather than a one-time benchmark download. It can fail as a procurement signal because the oracle only checks test outcomes (subtle bugs can slip through if feature and bug tests are weak), results depend heavily on the harness rather than the model alone, and a two-agent duel format is a research artifact with no production role for a small team. 2 independent implementations, 18 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Contextual Correction of Parallel Draftsfor Speculative Decoding
item.description: DCOCO replaces the top-1 commitment of parallel diffusion-based drafters (e.g., DFlash) by retaining multiple candidate tokens per draft position and scoring their contextual compatibility across adjacent positions in parallel, restoring intra-block dependencies without sequential drafting. It costs an additional lightweight correction stage per draft block, extra candidate storage, and integration into a diffusion-drafter serving stack, and it is not drop-in for conventional autoregressive speculative decoding. It can fail when the verifier or drafter backbone differs from the evaluated configurations, when the correction overhead erodes gains at low batch sizes, or when sequential correctors under load are the actual bottleneck it claims to avoid. 2 independent implementations, 149 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models
item.description: The method replaces the standard practice of serving a fixed-depth non-recurrent transformer (or maintaining separate checkpoints per accuracy/latency tier) with a single recurrently applied block whose loop count is chosen at inference, while removing the usual one-loop accuracy penalty through gated state updates, mixed loop counts in training, and loop-index conditioning. The cost is that the gains require modifying pretraining: the recipe must be trained in, and all reported results come from models the authors trained themselves, including a late-stage mixed-depth schedule that still adds training compute. It can fail for a constrained-infrastructure adopter because no pretrained foundation model can be retrofitted with ELR via fine-tuning alone with validated results, the accuracy-per-loop gains on downstream production workloads are unverified outside the authors' benchmarks, and multi-loop serving multiplies per-request latency and compute on a single 24 GB GPU where a 4B-class model is already near the practical ceiling. 2 independent implementations, 126 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.
